body.problem_statement: In Firefox, refreshing the dashboard after sign-in causes the next authenticated API call to return 401 even though the bearer token in localStorage is still valid. Chrome is unaffected.
body.summary: Firefox-only auth regression after page refresh. Token is present but not sent (or sent in a form the server rejects).
body.current_behavior: POST /api/me returns 401 immediately after refresh in Firefox 131.
body.expected_behavior: POST /api/me returns 200 with the user object as long as the bearer token in localStorage has not expired.
body.user_impact: All Firefox users are signed out on every refresh. Estimated 18% of active users.
body.business_impact: Increased support volume; risk of churn on the Firefox segment.
constraints: fix must not change the token storage location
non_functional_requirements: regression test must run in CI

acceptance_criteria.statement: After refresh in Firefox 131, the next /api/me call returns 200 when the token has not expired.

acceptance_criteria.verification_hint: existing chrome e2e suite remains green

acceptance_criteria.statement: No change to token storage shape or location.

assumptions: Server-side validation is correct; the regression is in the client.
risks: Naive fixes may add the header twice and break existing chrome behavior.
